pass_b_english: “You prepared a table before me, opposite those who afflict me; you anointed my head with oil, and your cup that makes drunk as strongest” (Psalm 22:5).

What does “opposite those who afflict me” want? It has some unspeakable mystery, that someone may pray to be afflicted. Think for me, just as in the great contests prizes lie upon each contest, so according to each affliction: whenever an afflicting is present, and the afflicting powers, the opposing ones, think for me a spiritual and intelligible table prepared through this affliction. As often, then, as you are afflicted, so often also a spiritual table is set beside you. Only have eyes that see my tables, that giving thanks you may say with the apostle: “And not only so, but also boasting in the afflictions” (Romans 5:3).

And in the beginnings we were saying that the one from progress encamps into a place of green grass; since then the one progressing, even if he should arrive at the end, no longer remaining a sheep, but having been shown rational, has a table of rational foods, made ready by the Lord … And give heed, whether also as long as someone is in this life, seeing the truth through a mirror and through a riddle, he is a sheep led under a shepherd; but having passed upon the coming age, applying face to face to the truth, he applies to a spiritual table, according to: “And I will covenant a covenant to you, to eat and to drink upon the table of the Father in the truth.” Whence also “you prepared” has been said, for from here God prepared the things which the eye has not seen, and so on. And “before me” shows that the table has been manifested to me and known to me, opposite those who afflict me, many wishing to be hostile to me.

And the Lord, wishing me through these who afflict me to rise strongly toward them, prepared a table before me, on which solid food lies, that having been filled with this athletically I may be able to stand against the afflicting nobly. For when we happen upon perfect good things, we have the opposing strong and more, as the apostle says: “For a great door has opened to me, and the opposing are many” (1 Corinthians 16:9).

And the one whose head is anointed with oil from the Lord will say: “Let not the oil of a sinner anoint my head” (Psalm 140:5), as being anointed from God with the oil of gladness, Christ. And I think that also when fasting he is thus anointed on the head, and the face is washed. And since not only a table, and so on.

choices.english: that someone may pray to be afflicted
choices.why: The mystery of ‘opposite the afflicting’ is that one may pray to be afflicted, because each affliction sets a table. OCR ι να τις ευ χηται.
rejected: that someone may pray never to be afflicted

choices.term: Ὁσάκις γοῦν ἐὰν θλιβῇς, τοσαυτάκις καὶ τράπεζά σοι παρατίθεται πνευματική
choices.english: as often as you are afflicted, so often also a spiritual table is set beside you
choices.why: Table frequency matches affliction frequency. Not ‘one table for all afflictions’.
rejected: the table is only after death

choices.english: and the one whose head is anointed with oil from the Lord
choices.why: OCR Ου δὲ is Ὃ δὲ, the one anointed from the Lord, not a negation.

the sinner’s oil is from the Lord
